_comment: The bundled first Daily Test (kDayZeroQuestions, lib/data/day_zero_daily_test.dart), exported with DailyTestQuestion.toJson on 2026-09-27 through a throwaway flutter test. Reference set R3 of the local measurement E: written and reviewed by hand, so every question is known good.
If the Dart constant changes, export it again; nothing checks the two against each other.

questions.context: You should avoid ___ too much sugar.
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct form of the verb in brackets.

commonWrongAnswers.comment: 'Avoid' is followed by the -ing form, not 'to'. Say 'avoid eating'.

questions.explanation: After 'avoid', the next verb takes the -ing form, so it's 'avoid eating'.

questions.context: She is best student in our class.
questions.instruction: Find the mistake and rewrite the full corrected sentence.
questions.correctAnswer: She is the best student in our class

commonWrongAnswers.answer: She is a best student in our class
commonWrongAnswers.comment: 'Best' is a superlative, and superlatives take 'the': there is only one best.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: She is best student in our class
commonWrongAnswers.comment: That is the same sentence. Look for the small word missing before 'best student'.

questions.explanation: 'Best' compares her with everyone else, and there is only one best, so it needs 'the': 'the best student'.

questions.instruction: Find the mistake and rewrite the full corrected sentence.

commonWrongAnswers.comment: After a modal like 'can', use the plain verb: 'can speak'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: She can to speak three languages
commonWrongAnswers.comment: Modals are followed by the plain verb without 'to'.
That is the same sentence. Look at the verb after 'can'.

questions.explanation: After 'can', the verb stays in its plain form, even with 'she', so it's 'can speak'.

questions.context: Tom said he ___ call me the next day.
questions.instruction: Put the verb in brackets into reported speech.

commonWrongAnswers.comment: After 'said' (past), 'will' moves back to 'would' in reported speech.
'Could' means 'was able to'. To report 'will', use 'would'.

questions.explanation: When you report what someone said in the past, 'will' moves back to 'would': 'he would call me'.

questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct form of the verb in brackets.

commonWrongAnswers.comment: With a finished time like 'yesterday', use the simple past: 'saw'.
'Seen' needs a helper verb. With 'yesterday', use the simple past 'saw'.
'Had seen' is for something before another past moment. With 'yesterday', use 'saw'.

questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' is a finished time in the past, so the verb goes in the simple past: 'saw'.
